findings.title: Removing the .title float rule changes header layout without replacement
findings.body: The diff deletes the `.title { float: left; }` rule from `.d-header .contents` and switches `.contents` to a flex container. Any `.title` element inside the header now loses its left float and is laid out only by flex defaults. Nothing in the PR shows that the markup no longer relies on this, so the header title position may shift or break on pages that render it.

findings.title: Panel float removed and replaced with flex ordering that is not verified
findings.body: `.panel` drops `float: right` and gains `margin-left: auto` plus `order(3)`. This only works if every sibling in `.contents` is a flex item with orders 1 and 2 set correctly. Siblings like `#site-logo` and `.icons` are not given any order, so the final arrangement depends on DOM order and browser support for the old `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` fallback. This needs checking in the rendered header.

findings.title: Bullet margin-top rule removed from extra-info badges with no replacement
findings.body: The `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule is deleted, and nothing else in the diff restores that spacing. Bullet category badges inside the extra-info wrapper will sit flush against the top of the line, a visible regression that the PR does not mention.

findings.title: Small-action description padding and margins changed without explanation
findings.body: `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` and `margin-top: 5px` to `padding: 0 1.5%`. The 4em left indent that offset the icon column is gone, and `p` margin and the `> p` padding-top are also dropped. The text will reflow and the vertical rhythm of every small-action post will change. The PR gives no reason for this and no visual check.

findings.title: Floats on children of a new flex container are ignored
findings.body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container, but its children `.topic-avatar` and the `button` (with float: right) keep their float rules. Floated flex items are ignored, so these float declarations no longer do anything. Either the floats are dead code or the layout was not checked after the switch to flex.

findings.title: inline-flex mixin emits multiple display values, including a legacy one
findings.body: The `.bullet` rule now uses `@include inline-flex()`, which emits several `display` declarations, including `-webkit-inline-box` and `-moz-inline-box` alongside `inline-flex`. Browsers that do not understand `inline-flex` fall back to the legacy value, which can change the badge box model in old browsers. The previous single declaration did not have this effect.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid property and passes unsupported values to legacy box-align
findings.body: `-ms-align-items` is not a real CSS property and is ignored. `-webkit-box-align` only accepts values like start, center, end, baseline, and stretch, so passing a flex-specific value such as flex-start through this mixin produces an invalid legacy declaration. The mixin also sets `-ms-flex-align`, which is the correct IE property, so the extra line is just dead output.

findings.title: Mixins added as a block after existing ones with no check for duplicates
findings.body: The flexbox, inline-flex, align-items and order mixins are appended here. If any of these names already exist in another stylesheet partial (for example the `order` mixin used in topic.scss), Sass silently redefines them, and the later definition wins. Nothing in the PR confirms that the names are unique or that the output of existing callers is unchanged.

findings.title: PR description is a placeholder and the title claims a performance gain
findings.body: The description says only 'Test 5', and the title says the change optimizes header layout performance. The diff is a set of visual layout rewrites with no measurement, no before/after comparison, and no statement of the intended rendering change. A reviewer cannot judge the risk without this context.
